revisions.title: The walk beyond the walls
revisions.body: Phaedrus comes from Lysias and walks outside the city wall to rehearse the speech; Socrates presents himself as following because he is eager to hear it. The Ilissus setting is immediately tied to Phaedrus's question about whether the Boreas story is true, bringing the physical walk into the dialogue's first question about myth.

revisions.title: Writing as a reminder, not a substitute
revisions.body: The Egyptian tale turns on a reversal: Theuth presents writing as a remedy for memory and wisdom, while Thamus says it produces forgetfulness and only the appearance of wisdom. Socrates later calls writing a reminder for one who already knows, then contrasts its helplessness when questioned with speech written with knowledge in the learner's soul, capable of defending itself. I hear this as a limit on what writing can do, not its disappearance.
